newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia, Estonia to sign stock depository deal.
newsitem.headline: Latvia, Estonia to sign stock depository deal.

text.p: Latvia's central stock depository said on Wednesday it would sign on January 31 a deal with the central depository of neighbouring Estonia to allow each country's stocks to be registered in their central depositories.
The agreement is the first cross-border registration deal in the Baltic states and is aimed at boosting trade in the countries' fledgling share markets.
"This agreement is significant in that it means that the Latvian central depository will fully enter into the international financial sphere," the Latvian depository said in a statement.
It also said that the agreement would mean that Latvian shares would also now become available for the investors of other countries.
Latvia's stock market opened in 1995 while Estonia's is one of the newest in eastern Europe, having only opened for business in May 1996.
